historical_evidence: Retain the immutable v4 protocol and all original lsof outcomes, warnings and failures. An unverified lsof snapshot remains unverified. New collector results require new identified reports and cannot retroactively repair those reports or be pooled with them.
scope: Replace only the macOS descriptor observation method in a separately identified implementation slice. Linux numeric /proc/PID/fd enumeration, owned unreaped child lifetime and v4 idle/after-warmup/200ms-postload collection points remain unchanged. No descriptor target, pathname, process name, user payload or raw diagnostic may be emitted or retained.
method: A development-only C helper uses the active macOS SDK libproc.h and sys/proc_info.h. Query PROC_PIDTBSDINFO before and after PROC_PIDLISTFDS and require matching requested PID/start seconds/start microseconds. Use size hint plus bounded growth retries, exact proc_fdinfo record alignment, nonnegative unique numeric descriptors and an owned live child. Do not silently reinterpret permission, exit, growth, malformed records, warnings or process-identity mismatch as an empty valid snapshot.
memory_bound: Compute the bounded record allocation with checked131072*sizeof(struct proc_fdinfo) from the active SDK. Refuse overflow, a required size beyond that allocation, a list whose buffer is full after the final retry, and a byte count not divisible by sizeof(struct proc_fdinfo). This is a collector bound, not a gateway allocation/retention measurement.
preconditions: Compile the helper with the already-required C toolchain outside every timed HTTP interval, record helper/source/compiler/SDK identity and use the ordinary bounded owned process runner. No new runtime dependency, unsafe Rust, privileged access or installed-user configuration change is required. Validate synthetic open/close lifecycle, process exit/identity mismatch, parser bounds, cancellation and failed compilation/invocation before collection.
result: Emit only schema/method/status/verified/count. Every unsuccessful or ambiguous collection has verified=false and count=null, with a fixed private-free status. A verified result is an identity-checked, non-atomic OS descriptor-list observation at one query, never an atomic peak or proof of long-term recovery.
timing_and_acceptance: Collection occurs outside the measured HTTP interval equally for both engines. Keep all inherited workload families and concurrency1/8/32/128,32GiB near-limit safety heuristic, sample counts, five paired alternating rounds, power/load record, CPU/request0.7,startup0.5,idleRSS0.6,large-catalog lifetime peak0.7,throughput0.9 and original p95/p99 rules unchanged. No new FD acceptance threshold is declared; counts and warm/postload deltas remain descriptive and require two verified observations. Missing allocations, retained-state soak, controlled hardware and other plan gates remain unmeasured.
